why:
phase-456 W9 — what `rclcpp::Client<S>::SharedPtr` names. Upstream's is a `std::shared_ptr<Client<S>>`; ours is a two-word `{executor, handle_id}` value, and the difference is not an optimisation. A client created with a RESPONSE HANDLER is owned by the Rust executor arena, which holds the `RmwServiceClient` and — since phase-456 W3 — the handler itself as its trampoline context. Nothing of the caller's is referenced after registration, so there is no C++ object for a pointer to point at and none is made.

IT IS THE ONE IN THE FAMILY THAT CARRIES A VERB, and that is a MEASUREMENT rather than a preference. W3's census across `examples/`, `tests/`, `book/` and `packages/`, re-measured on W9's base: a dispatch SUBSCRIPTION and a dispatch SERVICE have NOTHING invoked on them — stored and dropped, which is what `cpp:SubscriptionHandle` and `cpp:ServiceHandle` are — while a dispatch CLIENT has exactly one verb, `async_send_request`, at `examples/linux/cpp/service-client-callback/src/main.cpp:95` plus the move probe W3 added at `tests/compile/bind_service.cpp:139`. So a bare keep-alive would be one verb short here, and an `Owned<Client<S>>` would claim an ownership the arena holds. `{executor, handle_id}` is not bookkeeping on this type: it is the ARGUMENT LIST of `nros_cpp_service_client_send_on_handle`, which is why the verb fits on two words.

NO `operator->`, for the reason `cpp:SubscriptionHandle` gives — there is nothing at the other end — so a ported `client_->async_send_request(req)` is a compile error naming `ClientHandle` and the mechanical edit is one character. A self-returning `operator->` was rejected: it would have compiled that line by claiming a pointee that does not exist. Measured: no in-tree site writes `->` on a dispatch client handle.

The draining API a caller might have reached for is `nros::PollClient<S>`'s, on the half that owns a client.

UPDATED 2026-09-28 — STILL TWO WORDS, NOW THREE VERBS. `service_is_ready` and `wait_for_service` joined `async_send_request` when their FFI entry points gained the `(executor, handle_id)` arm (see `cpp:Client::wait_for_service`). No member was added: both read DISCOVERY state, so an arena index is the whole argument list, and the last line above — that the draining API a caller might reach for is `nros::PollClient<S>`'s — narrows to the four verbs that read CALLER STORAGE (`send_request`, `call`, `call_polling`, their `_sized` forms). The census is unchanged and still says ONE verb is INVOKED on a handle in-tree; what these two answer is what a PORTED node reaches for, which is upstream's own service tutorial opening with `wait_for_service`.
